steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The incarnation is the Christian belief that God became human in the person of Jesus Christ. "Incarnation" means "made flesh" — from the Latin "caro" (flesh).

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Be prepared to explain why the incarnation matters — it enables salvation (Jesus could bridge the gap between God and humanity), reveals God's nature, and shows God understands human suffering.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — The Incarnation
steps.body: 1. For The Incarnation questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of The Incarnation to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Explain two reasons why the incarnation is important for Christians. | Q: "Jesus was just a good teacher, not the Son of God." Evaluate this statement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
